detail.abstract: The U.S. trucking industry faces a structural workforce crisis characterized by persistent driver shortages and annual turnover rates exceeding 90 percent among large truckload carriersconditions that compensation-driven recruitment strategies have consistently failed to resolve. This study examines how data-driven recruitment marketing frameworks operate within this context, with particular attention to CDL driver acquisition. Drawing on academic recruitment theory, secondary industry data, and practitioner-level operational observations obtained through collaborative access to an active U.S.-based trucking carrier, the analysis develops an integrated framework across four dimensions: digital trust architecture, employer brand differentiation, recruitment channel strategy, and funnel performance analytics. The study argues that CDL driver recruitment is increasingly governed by marketing-system logic rather than traditional HR process-and that carriers which apply integrated recruitment marketing frameworks demonstrate measurable advantages in acquisition efficiency, applicant quality, and retention outcomes. Grounded in signaling theory (Spence, 1973), employer branding research (Backhaus & Tikoo, 2004), and recruitment process scholarship (Breaugh, 2013), the analysis demonstrates that digital trust signals function as conversion variables rather than reputational amenities, that employer brand differentiation reduces dependence on compensation-based competition, and that funnel analytics enable recruitment decisions to be evaluated with the same precision applied to customer acquisition systems. Structural characteristics of the trucking industry-including fragmented carrier landscapes, small-fleet dominance, and historically transactional hiring models-are examined as conditions that have slowed adoption of these frameworks while simultaneously amplifying their potential impact. The study contributes an industry-specific analytical framework for CDL recruitment marketing, positions practitioner observations within a theoretically grounded research design, and identifies directions for subsequent empirical investigation at greater organizational scale.

title: Overcoming Data Sparsity in Ride-Hailing Demand Prediction: A Transfer Learning Framework for Emerging Cities

detail.title: Overcoming Data Sparsity in Ride-Hailing Demand Prediction: A Transfer Learning Framework for Emerging Cities
detail.abstract: Accurate ride-hailing demand prediction is critical for fleet management and dynamic pricing, yet remains challenging in emerging cities where historical trip data are sparse or entirely absent. While deep learning models have achieved state-of-the-art performance in data-rich metropolitan areas, their effectiveness degrades sharply when transferred to cities with limited observations due to domain shifts in spatial layouts, point-of-interest distributions, and travel patterns. This paper proposes a transfer learning framework designed specifically for ridehailing demand prediction under extreme data sparsity in emerging urban contexts. The framework integrates three key components: (1) a spatiotemporal feature alignment module that learns city-agnostic representations from source cities with abundant data using adversarial domain adaptation; (2) a meta-learning initialization strategy that enables rapid fine-tuning with as few as 7-14 days of target-city data; and (3) a graph-based region embedding mechanism that encodes transferable road network and land-use features without requiring historical demand records. Experiments conducted on real-world trip data from three data-rich source cities and four emerging target cities across two continents demonstrate that the proposed framework reduces prediction error by 38-52% compared to training from scratch and outperforms existing domain adaptation baselines by 15-23% in terms of RMSE. Notably, with only one week of target-city data, the framework achieves accuracy comparable to models trained on three months of local data, offering a practical pathway for deploying intelligent mobility services in rapidly growing but data-scarce urban environments.

title: Nigeria's Net-Zero Ambitions And Coal-Fired Power Plants: Is There A Legal Prohibition?
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Nigeria's Net-Zero Ambitions And Coal-Fired Power Plants: Is There A Legal Prohibition?
detail.abstract:
Nigeria’s commitment to achieving net-zero greenhouse gas emissions between 2050 and 2070 has intensified debates regarding the compatibility of fossil fuel projects with the country’s climate obligations, particularly coal-fired power generation. This article critically examines whether Nigerian law expressly prohibits the construction and operation of coal-fired power plants within the framework of Nigeria’s net-zero ambitions. Through a doctrinal analysis of Nigeria’s mining, electricity, environmental, and climate governance regimes, the article evaluates the legal status of coal-fired electricity generation under existing statutes, regulations, policy instruments, and international climate commitments.

The article demonstrates that no Nigerian legislation currently imposes an outright prohibition on coal-fired power plants. The Nigerian Minerals and Mining Act 2007 permits coal exploration and exploitation, while the Electricity Act 2023 authorises electricity generation from both renewable and non-renewable sources, subject to regulatory approval. Likewise, environmental regulations issued by the National Environmental Standards and Regulations Enforcement Agency (NESREA) recognise fossil fuel-based energy projects and prescribe compliance standards rather than prohibitions. Significantly, Nigeria’s Energy Transition Plan contemplates the continued inclusion of coal-generated electricity within the country’s future energy mix, notwithstanding its decarbonisation objectives.

Notwithstanding the absence of a statutory ban, the article argues that coal-fired power projects in Nigeria face substantial regulatory, financial, political, and environmental constraints. The prevailing policy climate increasingly prioritises renewable energy development, while international financing institutions and commercial banks continue to retreat from coal financing due to global decarbonisation commitments. Furthermore, coal-fired projects are likely to encounter heightened environmental compliance obligations, public interest litigation risks, and regulatory hesitation arising from Nigeria’s climate commitments under the Paris Agreement and the Climate Change Act 2021.

The article concludes that Nigeria presently adopts a transitional and pragmatic approach to energy governance, balancing climate commitments with energy security and developmental considerations. Although coal-fired power generation remains legally permissible, evolving regulatory attitudes, market realities, and climate governance trends may render such projects increasingly impracticable in the long term.

detail.abstract: This paper examines the persistent gap between technology transfer and industrial development in West Africa, arguing that access to global technology alone is insufficient for sustainable economic transformation. Drawing on insights from Global Value Chain Theory, absorptive capacity, and technological capability frameworks, the study explores why integration into global production systems has not consistently translated into strong domestic industrial capacity. The paper situates West Africa within contemporary global production networks, where the region remains largely dependent on low-value activities such as raw material exports. It traces this challenge to colonial extraction systems and post-independence industrialization efforts that failed to develop deep technological capabilities. The study identifies a central paradox: despite increasing access to foreign technologies and industrial partnerships, domestic capacity to absorb, adapt, and innovate remains limited. Using case-based analysis, the paper contrasts unsuccessful industrial experiences with more promising developments, particularly the collaboration between the Dangote Group and ThyssenKrupp. It argues that sustainable development requires a transition from technology transfer to technological capability and ultimately industrial transformation. The paper concludes that West Africa's long-term development depends not merely on access to global technology, but on its ability to convert global knowledge into locally embedded industrial capability.

title: Forecasting the time of failure of tailings dams and Heap Leach Facilities through satellite InSAR data: myth or reality?
affiliations: University of Florence - Department of Earth Sciences, Norwegian Geotechnical Institute, Norwegian Geotechnical Institute, Norwegian Geotechnical Institute, University of Florence and University of Florence

detail.title: Forecasting the time of failure of tailings dams and Heap Leach Facilities through satellite InSAR data: myth or reality?

publicationDetails.detailsText: Remote Sensing Applications: Society and Environment, volume 42, 2026[10.1016/j.rsase.2026.101963]

detail.abstract: This paper addresses the complex challenge of forecasting the Time of Failure (ToF) for Tailings Storage Facilities (TSFs) and Heap Leach Facilities (HLFs) using satellite-based Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (InSAR) data. TSF and HLF structures can be susceptible to different failure modes, some of which can result in sudden instability due to the tailings' contractive and brittle behaviour. Moreover, the infrequent satellite passes can limit the ability to detect rapid changes or deformations in these structures, potentially reducing the effectiveness of monitoring efforts. Some recent papers propose predicting brittle failures in such structures using tertiary creep-based forecasting methods. However, this often requires a subjective procedure, and the results yielded are sometimes different and sometimes contradictory. To fully exploit the predictive potential of satellite InSAR data, a statistical multi-model methodology is introduced, with a primary focus on providing both quantitative estimates of the predictions and forecasting reliability. Through this methodology, different levels of warnings are issued. Low confidence alert would have been reached for Cadia up to 2 months in advance, whereas the highly confident one 12 days prior to the collapse. For Feijão moderate confidence alert would have been reached 39 days before failure. Special emphasis is placed on the evolution of failure risk in a simulated prospective manner, reproducing operational monitoring conditions. Our findings highlight the need for multiple technologies to accurately monitor such structures and justify the use of satellite InSAR for hazard screening.

title: 0DTE Options and the Price of Tail Protection
affiliations: City University of Hong Kong (CityU)

detail.title: 0DTE Options and the Price of Tail Protection
detail.abstract: On May 16, 2022, the addition of Tuesday and Thursday weekly expirations extended SPX same-day-expiry (0DTE) options to every weekday. SPX put skew compressed across tenors, peaking at 71 basis points at 30 days. A cross-tenor difference-in-differences design and the staggered identical 0DTE expansion in the Russell 2000 twenty months later rule out alternative drivers. Two reinforcing channels operate at distinct tenor bands: customer flow substitutes into pure-intraday 0DTE contracts at the short end, and dealer warehousing costs fall, with dealers absorbing more put-gamma at intermediate tenors. The implied annual reduction in the cost of equity tail insurance is approximately $1.4 billion. Post-2022 skew partly reflects intermediation-cost changes alongside tail-risk preferences.

detail.abstract: Microscopic traffic simulation models such as PTV VISSIM are widely used for operational analysis and evaluation. The efficiency and trustworthiness of these models depend strongly on careful calibration of driving behavior and related input distributions. Genetic Algorithms are used to calibrate the driving behavior parameters to mimic the real-life driving behavior. This paper proposes the Hall of Fame evolutionary framework offering a long-term memory as an alternative to the typical Genetic Algorithm. The paper compares the typical, shortterm memory, Genetic Algorithm with the proposed framework in terms of calibration speed. Data collected on a 3.15 miles corridor on I-64 in Saint Louis, Missouri and 5 years suggest that the Hall of Fame algorithm offers a faster calibration for the driving behavior parameters. In two scenarios, the proposed algorithm achieved lower errors than the typical algorithm in a short period of time.

title: Operationalizing Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) as a Sovereign Empowerment Rail to Mitigate Capital Flight and Resolve the Career Advancement Scheme Apparatus in India's Higher Education Ecosystem

detail.title: Operationalizing Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) as a Sovereign Empowerment Rail to Mitigate Capital Flight and Resolve the Career Advancement Scheme Apparatus in India's Higher Education Ecosystem
detail.abstract:
Background. India has constructed sovereign Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) for identity (Aadhaar), payments (UPI), document custody (DigiLocker), commerce (ONDC), and consent management (Account Aggregator). Despite a public higher education ecosystem comprising over 1,100 universities, 45,000 colleges, and a research workforce sustained almost entirely by taxpayer expenditure (UGC, 2024), validation of Indian scholarly output remains dominantly intermediated by foreign-controlled commercial publishing infrastructures (Ministry of Education, 2024; OECD, 2023).

Purpose. This paper conceptualises, doctrinally analyses, and econometrically evaluates Project SARASWATI, a proposed sovereign research-validation DPI designed to function as the missing "Research Layer" of India Stack. The paper interrogates how the Career Advancement Scheme (CAS) apparatus under University Grants Commission (UGC) regulations interacts with extractive Article Processing Charge (APC) regimes to produce a structural capital outflow, a fiscal paradox, and an institutional deadlock affecting Indian faculty, particularly in Maharashtra's state university system.

Methodology. The study deploys a multi-method framework integrating doctrinal legal analysis of the UGC Act, NEP 2020, and the National Research Foundation framework; institutional analysis of universities under Savitribai Phule Pune University, University of Mumbai, RTM Nagpur University, and Shivaji University; econometric modelling of APC outflows using publicly available pricing data from Elsevier, Springer Nature, Wiley, Taylor and Francis, MDPI, and Frontiers; comparative analysis with sovereign research initiatives in China, Germany, France, South Korea, and Brazil; and scenario modelling under five-, ten-, and 2047-horizon projections.

Findings. Conservative estimates place annual Indian APC outflows between USD 280 million and USD 460 million, with cumulative outflows toward 2047 plausibly exceeding USD 12 billion in nominal terms (author calculations from publisher annual reports; Springer Nature, 2024; Elsevier Annual Report, 2024). Faculty under CAS regulations confront a documented promotion deadlock created by the regulatory mandate for journal-indexed publications without sovereign provision of validation infrastructure. The Maharashtra state university system, and institutions of the Deccan Education Society, illustrate the micro-level operational pathology of this national policy gap.

Originality. This is among the first studies to model research validation as a DPI primitive, to draft statutory architecture for a sovereign validation rail, and to quantify the fiscal mathematics of academic capital flight under Indian conditions. The paper proposes a National Research Sovereignty Mission (NRSM) and provides a five-year implementation roadmap consistent with NEP 2020, Viksit Bharat 2047, and Atmanirbhar Bharat objectives.

Implications. Project SARASWATI is presented not as a publishing reform but as constitutional, fiscal, and infrastructural reform. Its operationalisation would advance research access equity, multilingual scholarship across India's twenty-two scheduled languages, and intergenerational knowledge sovereignty.

title: Debt Sustainability as a Recursive Compatibility Problem

detail.title: Debt Sustainability as a Recursive Compatibility Problem
detail.abstract:
Debt sustainability in private-sector fiat-credit economies is typically assessed through debt burdens, debt-service requirements, or repayment capacity. Yet these indicators may only partially characterize the conditions through which financial obligations remain recurrently serviceable over time.

This paper develops a circulation-based interpretation of debt sustainability centered on recursive compatibility and recurrent debt validation. Sustainability is conceptualized as a compatibility problem between outstanding financial obligations and the circulation and repayment conditions through which debt servicing remains recurrently feasible. A central implication follows: broadly similar debt environments need not imply similar sustainability conditions.

The empirical analysis uses quarterly data for eighteen advanced economies over 1999Q1–2023Q4. Conventional debt metrics explain only a limited share of subsequent debt-validation dynamics, while recursive compatibility contributes additional diagnostic information beyond broader structural benchmarks — differentiating sustainability conditions among economies facing comparable contemporaneous repayment burdens. The strongest empirical support emerges for subsequent debt-validation pressure, the outcome most directly implied by the framework.

The framework lends itself to real-time monitoring using publicly available macro-financial data. A pseudo-real-time application to 2007Q4 illustrates how recursive compatibility differentiates sustainability configurations across advanced economies immediately before the Global Financial Crisis, separating cases of hidden fragility from hidden resilience under broadly comparable observable pressure conditions.

More broadly, the findings suggest that similar observable debt conditions need not imply similar sustainability conditions. Recursive compatibility provides additional information about how financial obligations remain recurrently serviceable through time.

detail.abstract:
This preprint develops the concept of algorithmic abandonment as a critical and theoretical extension of social abandonment in contemporary digital society. It begins from Dr Cora M. Stack’s policy framework on loneliness, social abandonment, and Inclusive Community Belonging Hubs in Ireland, and uses Gretta Mohan’s ESRI-supported work on loneliness and mental health as an empirical Irish starting point.

The paper argues that digital capitalism, platform life, automation, artificial intelligence, and algorithmic identity systems do not merely intensify loneliness; they reorganise the conditions of belonging by replacing embodied presence with mediated, personalised, and data-producing forms of connection. It introduces the Algorithmic Abandonment Cycle as a six-stage framework and connects it to the IAAP model: Identity in the Age of Algorithmic Power.

The paper is conceptual and policy-oriented rather than empirical. It does not present new survey data, interviews, or clinical findings. Instead, it defines a new research problem, proposes operational indicators, develops future research propositions, and outlines policy principles for anti-abandonment and anti-capture design. Its central claim is that belonging should be treated as human infrastructure, and that digital tools should support embodied human connection rather than replace it.

title: Multinational Firms' Strategic Production Configuration with Considerations of Multilateral Tariffs and RCEP
affiliations: Sun Yat-sen University (SYSU), Sun Yat-sen University, University of Texas at Austin - McCombs School of Business and Sun Yat-sen University

detail.title: Multinational Firms' Strategic Production Configuration with Considerations of Multilateral Tariffs and RCEP
detail.abstract: In the context of escalating Sino-U.S. trade frictions and the implementation of the Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership (RCEP), many multinational firms (MNFs) are restructuring their global production networks by shifting manufacturing capacity from China to Southeast Asia. Motivated by this observation, we develop a model featuring three countries/regions-China, the U.S., and Southeast Asia-and a two-tier supply chain consisting of two competing MNFs and a key component supplier located in China. The model systematically examines MNFs' production location strategies under such a multilateral tariff environment. The two MNFs serve both the Chinese and U.S. markets and face a critical trade-off in production location decisions. Maintaining production in China secures local market advantages but results in higher export tariffs to the U.S. market. Conversely, relocating production to Southeast Asia lowers tariffs when exporting to the U.S., but makes exports to China subject to tariffs. Tariffs on exports to China are expected to decline gradually with the progressive implementation of RCEP. Our results show that MNFs have incentives to differentiate their production locations to alleviate global market competition. Their equilibrium production configurations-which may be symmetric or asymmetric-are primarily shaped by China's tariff disadvantage, global market conditions, and export tariffs from Southeast Asia to China. Interestingly, under certain conditions, further tariff liberalization under RCEP can induce MNFs to switch production locations twice: first from Southeast Asia to China, and then back to Southeast Asia.

title: Capital Markets LLM Reliability Score (CM-LRS): From Plausible to Bankable

detail.title: Capital Markets LLM Reliability Score (CM-LRS): From Plausible to Bankable

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author is a practitioner in investment banking working on AI and data systems. This research was conducted independently in a personal capacity and does not represent the views of any employer. The author has no financial relationship with, and received no compensation from, any of the model providers or vendors referenced. No models or vendors were evaluated under any commercial arrangement.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding and was conducted independently by the author.

detail.abstract: In capital-markets workflows, the question is rarely whether an LLM can produce a fluent draft. Today's frontier models will draft a debt-terms table, a comparable-transactions writeup, or an issuer profile that reads smoothly on first pass. The harder question is whether the draft is bankable: whether a banker, analyst, or compliance reviewer can defend it in front of a counter-party or a regulator, with the underlying documents in hand. Bankability requires the claims to trace back to verifiable source passages, the numbers to reconcile, the requested workflow to be completed in full, the model to have added nothing the source does not support, the output to be useful for a downstream decision, and the whole package to be verifiable by a domain expert in minutes rather than hours. Current LLM evaluation methods address parts of that gap but not the whole of it. Open-domain QA benchmarks reward surface accuracy. Finance-domain benchmarks (Fi-nanceBench, FinQA, ConvFinQA) advance document-grounded and numerical QA but evaluate at the question-answer pair layer. Multi-dimensional rubric studies of finance LLMs exist but are anchored on QA-style tasks rather than the workflow outputs bankers and analysts actually defend in front of reviewers, counter-parties, and regulators. This paper introduces CM-LRS, a Capital Markets LLM Reliability Score. CM-LRS evaluates LLM outputs at the workflow-output layer across seven reliability dimensions: factual accuracy, evidence traceability, numerical consistency, workflow completeness, source discipline, decision usefulness, and reviewability/auditability. Each dimension is scored 0-5 against a rubric anchored on practical signals reviewers in regulated environments actually use. The aggregate is tunable to the workflow under evaluation. We demonstrate CM-LRS on five representative capital-markets workflows: DCM transactionterms extraction, precedent retrieval, issuer profile synthesis, M&A transaction-comparable reasoning, and ECM transaction-terms extraction. All inputs are public: SEC EDGAR filings, a public UK takeover IR release, and obviously-fictional synthetic Nordic-style supplements to support strict reproducibility. We score outputs from four models: Claude Opus 4.7, GPT-5.5, Claude Sonnet 4.6, and the open-weights Llama 3.3 70B Instruct. Three findings of practical relevance for capital-markets buyers, established by scoring outputs against four independent LLM judges spanning three model families (Sonnet 4.6 and GPT-5.5 in-panel; Haiku 4.5 and Gemini 2.5 Pro out-of-panel) to control for self-and family-bias. First, the three frontier closed-source models cluster within a 0.22-point band on four-judge averaged CM-LRS (Sonnet 4.6 = 4.31, Opus 4.7 = 4.30, GPT-5.5 = 4.09); all four judges agree the open-weights baseline (Llama 3.3 70B at 3.15) is last. Second, the open-weights gap is concentrated on retrieval and synthesis class workflows, not extraction: under the primary judge the gap is 2.23 points on retrieval, 2.15 on synthesis, only 0.84 on the simplest extraction workflow. Third, Decision Usefulness (D6), the dimension that asks whether a reviewer would actually act on the output without major rework, shows the widest cross-model dispersion of any dimension in any workflow (a 4.0-point spread on the issuer-profile workflow alone) and sits in the top tier of inter-judge agreement (mean Pearson r = 0.52 across the six judge pairs, within 0.02 of the highest dimension). The combination is what makes D6 the cleanest dimension-level production-readiness signal in the rubric. Plausibility is cheap.  Bankability is the bar. CM-LRS is a deployment-readiness metric for high-stakes regulated environments, and is released with all rubrics, prompts, and demonstration tasks public.

title: The Impact of Chronic Workplace Stress on Employee Productivity and Efficiency

detail.title: The Impact of Chronic Workplace Stress on Employee Productivity and Efficiency
detail.abstract: In modern organizations, stress at work is a growing concern and has great effects on employee wellness and work efficiency (Colligan and Higgins 91). This study focuses on the effect of chronic occupational stress on productivity, efficiency, job satisfaction, absenteeism and organizational outcomes. The aim is to assess the correlation between chronic stress exposure and performance in the workplace and the impact of stress management techniques. In terms of methodologically, the study is based on secondary data, both qualitative and quantitative, which are obtained from peer-reviewed journals and organizational reports. The approach is a comparative analysis of stress related productivity outcomes in several industries such as healthcare, education, manufacturing and corporate services. This cross-sector vision enables one to gain a broader understanding of the different ways in which stress can present in the various contexts and demands of work. The results show that significant employee performance losses due to chronic work stress are not only in terms of their efficiency but also on their morale, creativity, physical health, absenteeism and organizational output (Daniel 377). But there is also some evidence that structured stress management programs (including employee assistance programs, workload restructuring, and wellness programs) can significantly affect productivity and employee well-being (Timotius and Octavius 194). To sum up, companies that make an effort to actively focus on employee stress reduction tend to have more engaged employees, better performance, and a more long-lasting productivity over time. The results emphasize leadership commitment and organizational culture as crucial factors in reducing stress-related risks and ensuring long-term productivity of the workforce.

title: Exploring Growth Mindset-Related Themes in Teacher Education Training of SY 2021-2022 English Pre-Service Teachers of CBSUA

detail.title: Exploring Growth Mindset-Related Themes in Teacher Education Training of SY 2021-2022 English Pre-Service Teachers of CBSUA
detail.abstract: The study examined how growth mindset-related themes were manifested in the reflective consciousness of the first batch of Enhanced K-to-12 English Pre-Service Teachers (PSTs) of the Central Bikol State University of Agriculture (CBSUA) Calabanga in the second semester of the school year 2021-2022. A meso-level qualitative research design, discourse and content analyses were used to analyze 30 reflective portfolios of 10 randomly selected fourth-year English PSTs, including their weekly internship logs and reflections on the Philippine Professional Standards for Teachers (PPST) domains. Data were analyzed using deductive thematic analysis and values coding based on an adapted framework of growth mindset indicators from Rutherford (2019). The analysis showed seven major growth mindset-related themes significantly intertwined with the training experiences of the PSTs: navigating role changes in teaching, learning from failures, dealing with personal limitations, and embracing challenges in the practicum.

title: The Crypt of the Symbolic: Signifying Absence, Narrative Desire, and the Limits of Sexual Ontology in Barthes's S/Z and Balzac's Sarrasine

detail.title: The Crypt of the Symbolic: Signifying Absence, Narrative Desire, and the Limits of Sexual Ontology in Barthes's S/Z and Balzac's Sarrasine
detail.abstract: To open Roland Barthes’s S/Z is to step into a textual labyrinth where the very notion of the book as a closed vessel of meaning is methodically dismantled. Barthes does not simply interpret Honoré de Balzac’s 1830 novella Sarrasine; he dismembers it into 561 fragments, or lexias, and traces through them the movement of five interweaving codes. This gesture is far more than a technical innovation in narratology. It is a philosophical intervention that recasts the act of reading as an encounter with the plural, the irresolvable, and the radically other. Barthes’s famous opening pronouncement — “the text is a galaxy of signifiers, not a structure of signifieds; it has no beginning; it is reversible; we gain access to it by several entrances, none of which can be authoritatively declared to be the main one” (Barthes, 1974, p. 5) — announces a shift from a hermeneutics of depth to a semiotics of surface and dissemination. In place of the critic who excavates a hidden truth, Barthes installs the reader as a producer of meaning, a subject whose desire is both solicited and perpetually deferred by the play of the codes. The choice of Balzac’s little-known tale is itself strategic: Sarrasine revolves around a secret that, once unveiled, does not resolve the narrative’s tensions but rather deepens them into an abyss of undecidability. A passionate sculptor falls in love with an opera singer whose radiant femininity is revealed to be a performance, a surface without the anticipated anatomical foundation. The body that should anchor the truth of sex becomes instead a void, a figure of radical alterity that collapses the binary of masculine and feminine and exposes the frailty of the symbolic order that relies on that distinction. The present essay undertakes a layered reading of Barthes’s reading, mobilizing the full theoretical apparatus of poststructuralism, psychoanalysis, feminist philosophy, and biopolitical critique to argue that the enigma at the heart of Sarrasine is not the mere secret of a disguised identity but the traumatic unveiling of the lack that constitutes all identity. Through an engagement with Lacan’s logic of the signifier, Derrida’s economy of the supplement, Irigaray’s critique of specularization, Kristeva’s analytics of abjection, Butler’s theory of performativity, Foucault’s genealogy of biopower, and the countersexual provocations of Paul B. Preciado, this essay will demonstrate that the “secret” of the narrative body is the truth of the symbolic itself: that the phallic function, far from being a substantial attribute, is a vacancy that organizes the field of meaning only through its veiling. Barthes’s S/Z, in this light, becomes a propaedeutic for a post-phallogocentric ethics of reading, an invitation to inhabit the text not as a solved equation but as an inexhaustible source of jouissance, a site where the binary machinery of gender and sexuality is both staged and subverted.

title: The Problem with Zero: How Xi's Pandemic Policy Created a Crisis for the Regime
affiliations: Johns Hopkins University

detail.title: The Problem with Zero: How Xi's Pandemic Policy Created a Crisis for the Regime
detail.abstract:
This is a preprint / author manuscript version of an essay published in Foreign Affairs. It is provided in text-only form and is not the publisher-formatted final version. The original publication is acknowledged and linked where available.

China's zero-COVID policy—rigidly enforced long after the rest of the world had adapted to the virus—was not primarily a public health strategy. Yuen Yuen Ang argues that it represented a paradigm-level governance failure rooted in the pathologies of overcentralized "directed improvisation." Once Xi Jinping personally staked his political authority on a singular numerical target, the bureaucracy abandoned adaptive problem-solving in favor of systemic gaming. Officials enforced draconian lockdowns not to optimize public health outcomes, but to maintain the leader's "holy zero."

Ang traces how directed improvisation—China's most effective governing mechanism under Deng Xiaoping, which successfully balanced top-down mandates with bottom-up experimentation—collapsed under Xi's rigid command-and-control apparatus. Exercising power as centralized as Mao Zedong's, yet armed with unprecedented high-tech state capacity, Xi engineered an environment of perverse bureaucratic incentives: enforcing zero-COVID yielded political rewards, while questioning it invited severe punishment. The November 2022 White Paper protests, marking the broadest cross-class mobilization since Tiananmen in 1989, exposed the accumulated socioeconomic costs of this governance breakdown. Outlining three potential scenarios for China's post-protest political trajectory, Ang concludes that Xi has inadvertently demonstrated the intrinsic value of limited freedom to the Chinese populace—scattering ideological seeds that will prove difficult for the state to uproot.

title: The Normalisation of Debt-Financed Status Consumption: Social Media, Household Saving, and the Behaviour of Young Urban India
affiliations: Ramrao Adik Institute of Technology, Navi Mumbai, India

detail.title: The Normalisation of Debt-Financed Status Consumption: Social Media, Household Saving, and the Behaviour of Young Urban India
detail.abstract: This paper examines how social media has reshaped the consumption and saving behaviour of young urban India, arguing that it has normalised a pattern of aspirational consumption that exceeds current income and is financed by instalment debt under conditions where that debt consumes a disproportionate share of earnings, erodes precautionary buffers, and blurs the boundary between what a household can afford and what it cannot. The analysis distinguishes consumption utility from signalling utility and locates the cost in the latter. Drawing on Reserve Bank of India household-savings data, Securities and Exchange Board of India retail-derivatives loss studies, the live-events and buy-now-paylater markets, and the regulatory record on financial influencers, the paper documents the pattern across five domains. Consequences are assessed in two stages: near-term household and life-cycle effects, and long-term macroeconomic effects as the cohort enters its primary earning years while the national savings pool remains below its pre-pandemic trend and the population ages. Three counterarguments are addressed. The paper concludes that the normalisation of debt-financed status consumption, under the conditions identified, is costly to households and constitutes a structural macroeconomic vulnerability for India.

detail.title: Interprofessional Knowledge Formation in Child Welfare Client Networks and Teams
detail.abstract: Clients in child welfare, who are facing complex life situations, often require support from interprofessional collaboration. This study examines how knowledge is formed differently in networkbased and teambased interprofessional work. The research is based on two datasets collected through focus group interviews, in which experts from social services, health care, and education, as well as experts by experience, discuss interprofessional collaboration and its significance in client services. Thematic analysis is employed to examine how professionals describe the formation of shared knowledge. The findings indicate that in both collaborative settings clientcenteredness and willingness to cooperate are fundamental to building shared knowledge. However, knowledge does not emerge automatically—it is shaped by a trusting atmosphere and by the temporal and spatial conditions of collaboration, which differ between teams and networks. These factors are also influenced by the boundaries produced by the organizations, which emerge in different model of interprofessional work. Networkbased knowledge formation is more strongly serviceoriented, whereas teambased work emphasizes interaction and collective reflection. In social work practice, it is essential to identify structures that enable collaboration and to strive for boundary-crossing modes of joint work that also strengthen a client-centered working culture.

title: The Silver Surfer Paradox
affiliations: Universitas Prasetiya Mulya

detail.title: The Silver Surfer Paradox

declarations.ethicsApproval: Independent doctoral research. Voluntary participation, anonymous, aggregated data only. Compliant with declaration of Helsinki principles

detail.abstract: This study examines the adoption of Generative AI in consumer pre-purchase information search among 1,597 Indonesian respondents surveyed in March 2026. Drawing on the Technology Acceptance Model and Diffusion of Innovation theory, the paper explores whether conventional age-based assumptions about technology adoption remain applicable in the context of consumerfacing Generative AI. The findings suggest a counterintuitive pattern: respondents aged 55 and above report the highest AI-first adoption rate in product search (24.2%), while the 25-34 cohort records the lowest rate (11.7%). This pattern is introduced as the Silver Surfer Paradox, referring to the unexpected tendency of older consumers to rely on Generative AI earlier or more directly than conventionally expected. A similar descriptive pattern appears across occupational categories, where managers, directors, C-Level executives, business owners, and independent professionals report higher levels of heavy AI use than staff-level employees. Rather than interpreting Generative AI adoption primarily as a function of demographic novelty-seeking, this paper proposes decision complexity as a plausible explanatory lens: consumers facing higher-stakes, multidimensional purchase decisions may perceive greater functional value in AI's ability to synthesize information. The study contributes exploratory evidence from an emerging market context and offers implications for consumer behavior theory, brand strategy, sales methodology, and AI Visibility Optimization (AIVO), particularly as firms seek to remain interpretable, citable, and recommendable within AI-mediated search environments.

title: The Association between Empathy and Burnout in Healthcare: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis across Professions, Specialties, Career Experience, and Empathy Domains

detail.title: The Association between Empathy and Burnout in Healthcare: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis across Professions, Specialties, Career Experience, and Empathy Domains

detail.abstract:
Background: Syntheses of the relationship between empathy and burnout are either outdated or do not examine potential differences across professions, specialties, or experience. We aimed to investigate the association between empathy and burnout in healthcare professionals, and explore differences by profession, specialty, experience, and empathy/burnout domains.

Methods: This systematic review and meta-analysis follows the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines, and was prospectively registered (PROSPERO: CRD420251075618). We searched APA PsycINFO, APA PsycArticles, CINAHL, The Cochrane Library, PubMed, and Scopus from inception to July 2025, alongside four grey literature databases. We included studies reporting correlations between empathy and burnout, measured by validated scales. Two independent reviewers screened studies and assessed risk of bias. The lead reviewer checked all data extraction. Empathy-burnout correlations were pooled using Fisher's z transformation with random-effects meta-analysis. Relationships between overall scales were included in the primary analysis. Subscale relationships between empathy (cognitive, affective, behavioural) and burnout (emotional exhaustion, depersonalisation, personal accomplishment) informed subgroup and exploratory analyses.

Findings: 116 studies were included and 38 (14,038 participants) contributed to the primary analysis. Risk of bias was high or critical in 98% of studies. Empathy was negatively associated with burnout (r=-0.21, 95% CI[-0.30, -0.12], p<0.001, I2=96.7%). There were no significant differences within professions, specialties, or experience. Behavioural empathy showed the strongest negative association with burnout (r=-0.35). Within affective empathy, associations differed significantly by burnout domain (p=0.001). Affective empathy was associated with higher feelings of personal accomplishment (r=-0.19), lower depersonalisation (r=-0.16), but had a negligible relationship with emotional exhaustion (r=0.06).

Interpretation: Higher empathy is associated with lower burnout across healthcare professions. Our findings challenge assumptions that empathy with patients increases burnout. Behavioural empathy may be particularly protective against burnout, suggesting that strengthening empathy skills could improve patient care and practitioner wellbeing.Funding​The Stoneygate Trust.

title: Seeing the Future, Selling the Present: AI-Generated Renovation Visualizations in Housing Transactions
affiliations: East China Normal University (ECNU), Tsinghua University - Hang Lung Center for Real Estate and New York University (NYU) - Leonard N. Stern School of Business

detail.title: Seeing the Future, Selling the Present: AI-Generated Renovation Visualizations in Housing Transactions
detail.abstract: Housing platforms now deploy generative AI to show buyers how a home might look after renovation. Unlike listing photos or VR tours, which reproduce a property's current state, AI-generated content depicts an unrealized future state whose market consequences are not well understood. Using proprietary data from a leading housing platform, we study AI-generated renovation visualization (AIRV), which renders plausible post-renovation interiors within the platform's VR interface. Our empirical analyses find that AIRV helps buyers imagine living in a home after renovation, with effects concentrated in listings whose post-renovation state is hardest to imagine, such as shell, never-occupied, and unfurnished units. Two opposing pathways drive these effects. Along the first, AIRV enhances perceived diagnosticity and increases onlineto-offline conversion, reflected in a higher showing-to-click ratio and shorter time to first offline showing. Along the second, AIRV raises buyers' pre-visit expectations, increasing the likelihood of expectation disconfirmation during in-person showings. The resulting bargaining frictions lengthen the post-showing phase and accelerate seller price discovery, as intensified buyer feedback prompts sellers to make larger list-price adjustments, leading to lower transaction prices for these hard-to-imagine listings. The expanded buyer pool and price corrections account for the higher sale probability. This work extends the literature by showing that AI-generated content's market effects propagate beyond the online stage and establishing a dual-pathway tension inherent in AI-generated future-state content, where the same content that accelerates online-tooffline conversion simultaneously introduces post-showing bargaining frictions that lower transaction prices. The findings inform platform design and governance of AIgenerated content in housing markets.

detail.abstract: Purpose-This paper introduces a five-layer compound supply chain vulnerability assessment framework calibrated to U.S. small and medium-sized manufacturers (SMMs). It addresses a gap created by the 2023 launch of the NIST Manufacturing Extension Partnership Supply Chain Optimization and Intelligence Network (SCOIN), which maps SMM supply chains to the sub-tier level but provides no method for converting those maps into quantified, comparable vulnerability scores. Design/methodology/approach-Grounded in Resource Dependence Theory, the Small Business Supply Chain Assessment Tool (SB-SCAT) operationalizes five vulnerability layersmaterial inputs (multi-tier), operational inputs, human capital concentration, financial buffer, and digital/cyber dependency-into a composite Small Business Supply Chain Vulnerability Index (SB-SCVI). Monte Carlo simulation (N=10,000) across four SMM archetypes generates SB-SCVI distributions. The index is cross-validated against U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA) disaster loan application data by sector and region. Findings-The compound SB-SCVI exceeds the sum of its layer-level components by a factor of 2.3 to 4.1 across archetypes, demonstrating that multi-layer compound assessment captures vulnerability that single-layer frameworks systematically understate. The human capital concentration layer, operationalized through the Key Person Concentration Index (KPCI), contributes disproportionately to compound vulnerability in specialized manufacturing SMMs where the owner-operator holds non-transferable tacit knowledge. SB-SCVI scores correlate with sector-region SBA disaster loan application rates, providing external validation. Research limitations/implications-Cross-validation relies on administrative disaster loan data as a proxy for realized disruption cost; future research should incorporate primary SMM survey data and longitudinal disruption tracking. Practical implications-The open-source SB-SCAT is designed for deployment through NIST MEP Centers under the SCOIN program, giving individual SMMs an actionable compound vulnerability score, a layer-level priority ranking, and a mitigation queue matched to federal support programs-at zero cost to the firm.

detail.abstract:
This paper develops a two-phase integrated model to simultaneously evaluate the fiscal viability and political persistence of a genuine Universal Basic Income (UBI) under private capital dynamics. In response to the methodological dissonance between macroeconomic orthodoxy, which rejects the proposal on grounds of static unviability, and pro-UBI approaches that appeal to political will as a closure mechanism, the paper proposes a positive political economy framework with predictive value.

Phase 1 demonstrates, through an impossibility theorem based on logical contradiction over the Government’s Intertemporal Budget Constraint, the structural unviability of a genuine UBI under the defined institutional domain. Automation irreversibly erodes labor tax bases while the indexed material sufficiency condition of UBI preserves it as a rigid real burden on output. This asymmetry generates a permanent and strictly positive structural primary deficit which, under endogenous sovereign risk conditions (r > g), prevents the State from generating the future surpluses required to sustain the initial debt stock, thereby violating the transversality condition.

Phase 2 translates this continuous imbalance into a discrete two-player dynamic game between the Incumbent and the Opposition under Markov Perfect Equilibrium. The model shows that UBI can persist politically while fiscal fragility remains below an endogenously derived threshold linked to the Domar condition. Illustrative empirical calibration suggests a finite persistence window of approximately 4.6 years for highly leveraged European economies and 20.8 years for wealthy economies with deep financial markets before forced adjustment, sovereign default, degradation of policy genuineness, or inflationary monetization emerges as the likely resolution mechanism.

title: Who Leads? Relative Age Effects on Social Capital
affiliations: Harvard University and Facebook

detail.title: Who Leads? Relative Age Effects on Social Capital
detail.abstract: This paper studies the causal effect of being the oldest within a school cohort on social capital. Using a fuzzy regression discontinuity design and data from Facebook, we find that boys who are older than their classmates make 11% more friends in high school. This social advantage is associated with leadership roles, with relatively older boys 42% more likely to become class president than their relatively younger peers. Men who were relatively older during childhood have larger social networks in adulthood, and disproportionately sort into management and entrepreneurship. Our findings suggest that small age differences in peer composition can have persistent effects on social and economic outcomes.

title: What Truly Drives Performance for Japanese Firms Today?

detail.title: What Truly Drives Performance for Japanese Firms Today?
detail.abstract: This study investigates the determinants of financial performance of Japanese firms over the past decade. Following the prior discussion of upper echelons and institution-based perspectives, we incorporate CEO, headquarters location, industry, firm factors, and year effects and conduct variance component analysis to predict the determinants of financial performance. The results show that the determinants of financial performance of firms vary among different types and industry, firm and CEO factors play major roles in contributing to the financial outcomes, while we do not find any locational effects in this empirical setting. This finding emphasizes the importance of multilevel perspectives in strategic management research.

detail.abstract: Geothermal energy holds vast potential for decarbonizing the U.S. energy system, yet the sector remains significantly underdeveloped, supplying only 0.4% of the nation's electricity. A principal barrier to growth is the fragmented and ambiguous legal landscape currently governing ownership of geothermal resources: thirty-three states lack any clear statutory or common-law framework identifying who owns subsurface thermal energy. This Article examines the physical characteristics of geothermal energy, recent developments in the U.S. geothermal sector, and the principal doctrinal approaches that might govern ownership of subsurface heat, including the ad coelum doctrine, common-pool and open-access frameworks, the rule of capture, and public ownership. It argues that geothermal energy’s fugacious, nonexcludable, and variably renewable nature makes conventional place-based private ownership difficult to justify or administer. The Article therefore advances two distinct models: (1) a regulated ownership-upon-capture regime, borrowed from oil and gas law, that treats geothermal heat as unowned until extracted; and (2) a public-ownership model that vests the resource in the relevant state or federal government while enabling secure, transferable use rights. Either approach, if paired with streamlined but robust regulation and clear access rules, could reduce legal uncertainty, protect land rights, attract capital, and support sustainable geothermal expansion nationwide and long-term energy security.

title: Automation, Alignment, and the Cooperative Interface

detail.title: Automation, Alignment, and the Cooperative Interface
detail.abstract: The paper demonstrates that social alignment is distinct from value alignment as it is currently understood in the AI safety literature, and argues that social alignment is an important research agenda. Work provides an important example for the argument, since work is a cooperative endeavor, and it is part of the larger manifold of social cooperation. These cooperative aspects of work are individually and socially valuable, and so they must be given a central place when evaluating the impact of AI upon work. Workplace technologies are not simply instruments for achieving productive goals, but ways of mediating interpersonal relations. They are aspects of a cooperative interface i.e. the infrastructure by which we engage cooperative behavior with others. The concept of the cooperative interface suggests two conjectures to foreground in the social alignment agenda, motivated by the experience of algorithmic trading and social robotics: that AI impacts cooperation through its effects on social networks, and through its effects on social norms.

title: Agriculturally modified recharge accelerates redox-driven arsenic mobilization in a shallow Mekong Delta aquifer

detail.title: Agriculturally modified recharge accelerates redox-driven arsenic mobilization in a shallow Mekong Delta aquifer
detail.abstract: Arsenic (As) contamination of groundwater poses a major health risk to millions of people worldwide, particularly in deltaic aquifers, yet the role of agricultural recharge in modulating As mobilization remains incompletely understood. This study investigated groundwater As dynamics along a river–inland transect in a known As hotspot of the Vietnamese Mekong Delta (VMD) using five shallow monitoring wells sampled monthly from March 2023 to November 2024. Time-series hydrochemistry was integrated with groundwater-level monitoring, sediment characterization, mineralogical analysis, conservative tracers, redox-sensitive species, As speciation, dissolved gas indicators (CO₂, CH₄, and SF₆), and trend analysis. Groundwater was strongly reducing and highly enriched in As. Total dissolved As increased from 289 ± 15 µg L⁻¹ at the river-proximal well to 656 ± 49 µg L⁻¹ at KA-W2 and 826 ± 43 µg L⁻¹ at KA-W3, reaching 960 ± 61 µg L⁻¹ at KA-W4 before decreasing to 802 ± 41 µg L⁻¹ at KA-W5. As occurred predominantly as As3+, accounting for ~89% of total dissolved As, consistent with reductive mobilization from iron(oxyhydr)oxides. As variability was not controlled by seasonal variation, redox state, or river proximity alone. Sediment and mineralogical data indicate that organic-rich Holocene deposits containing Fe oxides/hydroxides provide reducing capacity and reactive As-bearing phases, whereas sandy intervals and spatially variable fine-grained cover allow surface-derived recharge to influence shallow groundwater chemistry. Elevated Cl and Cl/Br signatures, together with NH₄ enrichment, indicate agriculturally modified recharge in seasonal crop areas. Correlation, trend, and dissolved gas data suggest that agricultural recharge enhanced redox progression along short flow paths. Time-series data also revealed As3+–Fe²⁺ decoupling, indicating that dilution, mixing, and mineralogical re-partitioning can obscure the relationship between dissolved As and ongoing Fe reduction. These findings identify agricultural recharge as a context-dependent redox modifier and highlight the need for land-use-aware, temporally resolved monitoring of As-prone groundwater systems.

title: BLAST: Bottleneck-Free Large-Scale Algorithm Scheduling Throughput A Streamlined Approach to the Flexible Job Shop Problem (FJSP)
affiliations: Sagesse University, American University of Science and Technology and Antonine University

detail.title: BLAST: Bottleneck-Free Large-Scale Algorithm Scheduling Throughput A Streamlined Approach to the Flexible Job Shop Problem (FJSP)
detail.abstract: The Flexible Job Shop Scheduling Problem (FJSP) is an NP-Hard problem for task sequencing and resource allocation that poses a computational challenge universally across scientific disciplines and industries that need optimal and fast, high-throughput schedules. The impact of FJSP scheduling solutions is deeply embedded in manufacturing and logistics, genomics and sequencing, astronomy and healthcare, with applications in supply chain optimization, telescope array observation schedules optimization, and hospital scheduling for patient flow. Our proposed BLAST algorithm (Bottleneck-Free Large-Scale Algorithm Scheduling Throughput), addresses this need at its core, relying on a novel hybrid approach overcoming the combinatorial complexity inherent to FJSP problems. BLAST can solve large-scale FJSPs deterministically, yielding optimal schedules and resource allocation efficiency in record time. BLAST is a hybrid method that relies on a combination of intelligent heuristics (Filter Beam Search and Local Search), which yield a quick, nearly optimal schedule that is subsequently used by an MIP solver (Gurobi) as a warm start solution. As a consequence, BLAST deterministically solves FJSP problems (to optimality) dramatically faster than any previously reported methods, using standard and commercially available hardware. BLAST’s optimized heuristics are intelligently guided by Linear Relaxation, greatly reducing the solution space and enabling Gurobi's MIP solver to quickly reach optimal schedules. The BLAST algorithm stands out for its breakthrough performance, solving to optimality 'Makespan Minimization' cases of complex benchmarks like the MK15, in well under 5 minutes, never so far accomplished in under 20 minutes. The flexibility of BLAST extends to other single objectives apart from Makespan Minimization, namely Total Processing Time and Total Tardiness minimization, as well as multiple weighted objectives, making it highly adaptable. Our BLAST algorithm breaks apart decades-old barriers in solving Flexible Job Shop Scheduling Problems to optimality, by introducing a ground-breaking approach that achieves optimal schedules within record-breaking run times, so far largely unattainable.
